title: Implement immutable audit sinks and evidence pipeline for admin actions and config changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an immutable (WORM-style) audit sink and automated evidence/reporting pipeline for admin actions, privileged access events, and configuration changes. The feature must meet data residency constraints (region-locked storage for Private/VPC customers), produce tamper-evident audit objects, and automate daily/onsite evidence bundles for compliance reviews.

Goals: 1) Ensure all admin actions (console, API, CLI), RBAC changes, policy updates, and key config diffs are captured with sufficient context to support chain-of-custody investigations. 2) Store audit artifacts in append-only, retention-locked buckets (or compatible object stores) with integrity hashes and signed manifests. 3) Provide APIs and Console views to fetch signed evidence bundles and a scheduled reporter that publishes digest bundles to customer-designated sinks (S3/GCS/Azure) and to an internal immutable archive for Redwood compliance. 4) Support private deployments: allow customer-managed object stores and KMS while proving audit integrity to Redwood controls team.

Constraints and non-goals: This ticket focuses on the server-side sink and evidence pipeline; it does not implement fine-grained UI filtering or long-term analytics (separate analytics ticket). We will not build a custom blockchain; integrity is achieved via signed manifests, object checksums, and append-only storage with retention locks.

Design notes: - Event model: structured JSON entries with fields: event_id (UUID v4), ts_utc (ISO8601), actor_id, actor_type (user/service), org_id, target_resource, action_type, change_delta (diff or full snapshot), request_context (IP, region, user_agent), related_request_ids, and schema_version. - Sink pipeline: 1) Event capture -> validation & enrichment (policy tags, residency tag) -> transform to canonical audit object -> push to buffer queue (Kafka/Rabbit) -> objectizer service packages events into time-ordered shards (hourly) -> compute SHA-256 per-object, append signed manifest containing object hashes and previous-manifest-hash (chaining) -> write to target object store with retention lock enabled. - Integrity: service signs manifests with Redwood signing key or customer-provided signing key (private deploy). Each manifest includes chain hash + list of objects + retention metadata + residency region claim. - WORM semantics: Use provider retention lock / Object Lock (S3) or equivalent; if not supported, emulate append-only by using unique immutable prefix + encryption key access controls + legal-hold metadata. - Evidence automation: nightly job builds evidence bundles for date ranges, verifies manifest chain, produces a signed report (PDF + JSON), stores bundle to customer sink and notifies via webhook/email. - Access & retrieval: read-only audit API that returns signed manifests and objects; Console adds an Evidence export action which requests pre-signed, time-limited download links for bundles. - Security: KMS integration required; keys used for signing must be HSM-backed in enterprise/private deployments. RBAC for who can request exported evidence must be enforced.

Performance/scale: Produce shards with a target size of 64MB to 256MB to optimize for S3 throughput and reduce object count at scale. Benchmark target: sustain 50k events/sec across multi-tenant hosted clusters with p99 write < 300ms (for capture+buffering). Storage cost controls: lifecycle policy to tier older bundles to Glacier/Coldline with retention metadata preserved.

Compatibility: Should support AWS S3, S3-compatible (MinIO), GCS, and Azure Blob. For Private deployments customers can provide endpoint and credentials; we will validate required features (retention lock supported or fallback strategy).

Rollout plan: Prototype in staging using Redwood-managed S3 with retention lock, run red-team tamper attempts and integrity verification, then enable for opt-in Private tenants, followed by GA for Dedicated/Hosted with configuration flags and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Captured events include required schema fields (event_id, ts_utc, actor_id, change_delta) and residency metadata
Artifacts written to target object store are immutable (retention lock or equivalent) and contain SHA-256 checksums
Manifests are signed and chained; verification routine validates chain for a date range and detects tamper
Evidence reporter runs nightly and publishes signed bundles to customer-designated sinks and internal archive
Audit API returns signed manifest and allows retrieval of evidence bundles; Console export action triggers the same flow
End-to-end tests for S3, MinIO, GCS, and Azure Blob pass in CI with simulated retention-lock and fallback behaviors
Private deployment supports customer-provided signing key and KMS configuration with documented setup steps
Security review completed and threat modeling notes addressed (key management, replay/rollover, access controls)
milestones: Prototype objectizer + manifest chaining in staging
Private deploy integration and customer install docs

comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Design review completed. Agreed on chaining manifests and supporting customer signing keys for private deployments. Action: Marco to prototype objectizer.

2026-03-03 - Marco Diaz: Prototype objectizer committed to feature branch. Initial shard format uses hourly sharding; object size targets need tuning after perf runs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1284

2026-03-04 - Lena Fischer (Security): Reviewed threat model. Raised concern about signing key rotation and long-term key archival; recommended HSM-backed keys and rotation policy. Added follow-up task for key rotation automation.

2026-03-05 - Marco Diaz: Integration test for S3 Object Lock passed in staging. Implemented manifest chaining with previous_manifest_hash field. Draft PR for manifest verifier: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1297

2026-03-06 - Product NOTE (Rohit Menon): Ensure evidence reporter supports data residency per-customer; add acceptance criteria for region-tag verification. Scheduling a customer-facing doc review with Legal next week.
